title: Hand Off to the Manager
subtitle: Capture the manager's acknowledgement
scenario: It is SD-1, 5:30 PM. The package is assembled; now it goes to the person who owns the new hire's first day. Deliver it to the hiring manager and capture their acknowledgement. A delivery nobody confirmed is not a handoff.
input: The Day-One Package for hire H-4021 is ready. It is delivered to the Hiring Manager for acknowledgement the evening before the start (SD-1). Capture who acknowledged it, that they confirmed the hire is ready, and when.
instructions: Record who acknowledged the package (the hiring manager).
Confirm they acknowledged the hire is ready.
Validate to mint the acknowledgement record.

fields.label: Acknowledged by
fields.explain: The hiring manager owns the new hire's first day; they are the one who acknowledges the package, not People Ops or the recruiter.

fields.label: Ready confirmed
fields.explain: The acknowledgement is the manager confirming the hire is ready; without it the delivery is unproven.

fields.label: Acknowledged at
fields.explain: Acknowledging the evening before (SD-1) leaves time to fix a surprise; a start-day acknowledgement is too late to react.

copilotPrompt: Capture the manager handoff for onboarding: who acknowledged the Day-One Package, that they confirmed the hire is ready, and when (the evening before the start).
successMessage: Handoff acknowledged. The hiring manager confirmed the hire is ready the evening before day one.

intro.heading: Before the archive: an accountable receipt

sections.title: Delivery is not the same as handoff
sections.body: Sending the package is not the end. A handoff is complete only when the receiver acknowledges it. The hiring manager's confirmation is what makes the hire truly owned on day one.

sections.title: Who owns day one
sections.body: People Ops and IT provisioned the hire, but the hiring manager owns their first morning. The acknowledgement transfers ownership cleanly to the person who greets them Monday.

sections.title: The evening before matters
sections.body: Acknowledging on SD-1 leaves a window to fix a surprise. If the manager spots a gap the night before, there is still time; on the start morning there is not.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: An acknowledgement record that closes the delivery loop and gets archived with the run - proof the manager confirmed readiness.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd send the readiness summary to the manager and wait for a 'got it, looks good' reply before considering onboarding closed.

an approval card carrying the package summary; the reply is captured on the run

takeaway.heading: Handoff acknowledged
points: You captured the hiring manager's acknowledgement of the package.
The manager confirmed the hire is ready - the delivery is now proven.
Acknowledging on SD-1 leaves time to fix a surprise before day one.
Ownership of the first day passed cleanly to the hiring manager.
The workflow can now close onboarding with an accountable receipt.
